name: RecurKit – Recurring Events for The Events Calendar
author: marcos0811258

sections.description:
RecurKit works with the free The Events Calendar. Churches, clubs, libraries, studios and community centres that run a weekly service, class or meetup can create the event once instead of copying it by hand every week.

How it works

  1. Open an event and find the Repeat box in the editor (block editor and classic editor).
  2. Tick Repeat this event, choose the weekdays, and end it after a number of occurrences or on a date (up to 52 per series).
  3. Publish. RecurKit creates each occurrence as an ordinary event through The Events Calendar’s own API, copying the times, venue, organizers, categories, tags and featured image.

Manage a series under Events > Series:

  • See every series with its rule, its next date and how many events it has.
  • Edit one occurrence in the normal event editor.
  • Edit an occurrence and every later one at once: title, start and end time, venue and description. Later occurrences that differ from the one you edit are listed first and keep their own values unless you choose to overwrite them.
  • Delete a whole series.

Occurrences are normal events. They show in every calendar view, can be edited one by one, and stay in place if you remove RecurKit.

RecurKit is an independent plugin. It is not made by or connected to the developers of The Events Calendar. “The Events Calendar” is used only to say which plugin RecurKit works with.

A separate paid add-on, RecurKit Pro, adds monthly rules (for example “2nd Tuesday”), custom date lists, skip dates, a time shift for a whole series and series longer than 52 occurrences. Everything described above is free and stays free. See RecurKit Pro for plans and prices.

New to recurring events in The Events Calendar? Read how to make recurring events with the free The Events Calendar.

This plugin makes no external calls and collects no data.

Privacy

RecurKit for The Events Calendar makes no external calls, sets no cookies and collects no personal data. On uninstall it removes its own recurkit_ options and _recurkit_ event data, and deletes generated events only if you chose that.
sections.installation:
1. Install and activate the free The Events Calendar plugin.
  2. Upload the recurkit folder to /wp-content/plugins/, or install RecurKit from the Plugins screen, and activate it.
  3. Edit any event and use the Repeat box. Series are listed under Events > Series.

While RecurKit is active it hides The Events Calendar’s “Need Recurring Events?” banner in the classic event editor, since the Repeat box covers weekly repeats.
sections.faq:
Does it need The Events Calendar?

Yes, the free The Events Calendar. Without it RecurKit shows one notice and does nothing else.

Does it change The Events Calendar’s database tables?

No. Every occurrence is created, edited and deleted through The Events Calendar’s own functions, so its tables stay consistent.

Can I change the rule of an existing series?

Not in this version. Edit later occurrences from Events > Series, or delete the series and create it again with the new rule.

What happens when I uninstall it?

Under Events > Series you choose what happens: keep the generated events as ordinary events (the default), or delete them. The events you created yourself always stay. RecurKit’s own settings and data are removed either way.

Does it send data anywhere?

No. It makes no external calls and does not track you.
sections.changelog:
0.1.2

  • Fix: Events > Series “this and later occurrences” no longer copies the first occurrence’s title, description or venue over later ones when you pick a later “Starting from” date and change only the time. Picking a date now reloads the form with that occurrence’s values.
  • Fix: “this and all later occurrences” no longer silently overwrites a title, description, time or venue you edited on a later occurrence. The form lists occurrences that differ from the one shown and keeps their values unless you tick the box. Where a field varies in the series, it also lists the later occurrences that will change with the one shown, and refuses to save if the series changed after the form was opened.
  • Fix: backslashes, which block editor markup uses, are no longer lost when RecurKit creates or updates occurrences. Copies made by earlier versions are not repaired: where they differ, the series form lists them, and with the box ticked they take the next change you make to that field.
  • Fix: saving the series form no longer treats an untouched description with line breaks, or a title with “&”, as changed.
  • Fix: when the event itself is not on a chosen weekday, it no longer counts toward “After N occurrences”, and the Repeat box warns and names the next matching date.
  • The Repeat box now sits right after The Events Calendar’s event details in the classic editor.
  • While RecurKit is active, The Events Calendar’s “Need Recurring Events?” banner is hidden in the event editor.

0.1.1

  • Readme and plugin header only: plugin name now starts with what it does, a homepage link and two links to brightlabs.app. No code change.

0.1.0

  • Initial release.
